summary: Source-anchored research for Salesforce Pub/Sub case alerting. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Automatic CDC generation is not an absolute no-loss guarantee: Salesforce documents rare cases where change messages are not persisted, delivered, or recoverable. Avoid presenting CDC-based Case alerts as transactionally guaranteed delivery. (low confidence)
Event Relay is a managed path from Salesforce platform events and change data capture events to Amazon EventBridge; it is not a direct relay to arbitrary brokers. (high confidence)

Event Relay is a Salesforce-managed subscription that delivers events to Amazon EventBridge. It provides basic relay monitoring; EventRelayFeedback exposes relay status and errors. (medium confidence)

Kafka is an external-broker alternative: Confluent documents a fully managed Salesforce Source V2 connector with Pub/Sub CDC ingestion, while OSO publishes an Apache-2.0 Kafka Connect suite with Pub/Sub CDC streaming. These are separate connector choices. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

Pub/Sub API is not a transport-only replacement for every legacy Streaming API subscription: it supports change data capture and high-volume platform events, but excludes PushTopic events, generic streaming events, and standard-volume platform events. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

A Pub/Sub CDC update is not a full record snapshot: unchanged fields are present with empty values even when the stored record contains values. Determine changes from decoded changedFields and distinguish actual clearing from unchanged placeholders with nulledFields. (high confidence)

The community explanation of CDC states that events do not contain old values; the official body documentation describes updates using changed values and empty unchanged fields. Therefore, qualification of a particular old-to-new severity transition requires a previously maintained value or another explicit source of prior state; querying the current record after delivery does not recover the event’s old value. This state requirement is a design inference from the two sources. (medium confidence)

Salesforce’s January 2021 example bridges CDC events to an autolaunched Flow through an Apex trigger; a March 2021 community answer independently proposes invoking Flow from Apex. These sources establish a historical implementation pattern. (medium confidence)
The CDC-to-Flow example uses an `after insert` event trigger and requires bulkification because the trigger can receive a list of events. (low confidence)

Salesforce documents Flow action transaction control starting in Winter ’26. Record-triggered flows can apply it on asynchronous or scheduled paths, but not the immediate path. A callout with pending operations fails if the action always continues in the current transaction. (low confidence)

Lightning after-save Flow triggers can initiate SOAP outbound messages. Salesforce generates a WSDL for the external listener and dispatches messages through a local background process. (low confidence)

Salesforce’s asynchronous-processing guide says outbound messages from an after-save Flow remain queued until delivery succeeds or they are dropped after 24 hours of unsuccessful delivery. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

For DML-initiated Apex triggers, remote calls must execute asynchronously from the initiating event. Salesforce also supports a declarative HTTP Callout action in Flow, so HTTP delivery and SOAP outbound messaging require separate design choices. (low confidence)

Apex change-event triggers execute outside the transaction that published the change event, but use synchronous Apex governor limits. The default running identity is Automated Process; PlatformEventSubscriberConfig can override the running user and batch size. (low confidence)

Bulkify CDC trigger handlers: Salesforce’s example warns that the trigger receives a list of events, and the developer guide documents a maximum batch of 2,000 event messages. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

For record-triggered Flow actions, transaction controls apply to asynchronous or scheduled paths, not the immediate path. With Let the flow decide, a callout with pending work commits the current transaction and runs in a new one; Always continue in current transaction instead fails in that situation. With Let the flow decide, debugging keeps the action in the current transaction. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

SOAP outbound messages can be initiated by an after-save Flow. Delivery uses a local scheduled background process and OutboundMessage records, separate from the asynchronous Apex queue; executing the Flow action does not send the message synchronously. (low confidence)

Asynchronous Flow execution has no SLA and can have unpredictable wait times. An asynchronous path keeps work off the initiating transaction’s critical path, but does not establish a fixed alert-delivery deadline. (low confidence)

For outbound Apex callouts initiated from a data-change trigger, Salesforce’s integration guide requires asynchronous execution from the initiating event. The async decision guide recommends Queueable Apex over future methods and warns that finite asynchronous threads can delay outbound integrations. (medium confidence)

For a specific old-to-new severity transition, maintain prior values in the consumer’s persistent store or consult field history when that field is tracked; querying the already committed record alone does not restore its previous values. This is a design inference from the documented payload and commit semantics. (medium confidence)

Custom alert publishing must cover every relevant write path. SFHooks specifically warns that data-loader changes, API edits, and packages can be missed when those paths forget to publish. (low confidence)

CDC stream filtering reduces event delivery allocation usage because usage counts events delivered after filtering. This scopes the argument that every subscriber must receive every record change. (high confidence)
Custom Platform Events let an application define the payload schema and publish business signals from Apex, Flow, or an API. Defining the event alone does not publish those signals. (high confidence)

For custom Platform Events published within Salesforce transactions, Publish After Commit publishes only after a successful commit and suppresses publication when the transaction fails. The setting does not apply to messages published with Pub/Sub API. (low confidence)

Treat routing readiness as a separate condition from Case lifecycle alert eligibility. This is an architectural inference: Omni-Channel applies routing logic when work is assigned to an owner and does not reapply it after later field edits; PendingServiceRouting describes work waiting for routing or assignment. (medium confidence)

For queue-based routing, PendingServiceRouting creation does not invoke before-insert or after-insert triggers, or actions such as triggers, workflow rules, or validation that could interfere with record creation. A design that expects an insert trigger on this routing record to deliver every alert conflicts with this documented behavior. (low confidence)

Streaming API pushes available events without client control of the delivered count. Pub/Sub API lets the consumer request a count based on its processing capacity, providing subscription flow control. (high confidence)

Pub/Sub CDC headers include changedFields and nulledFields that Streaming API omits; nulledFields, diffFields, and changedFields require further processing. Consumers must account for this header difference when migrating. (low confidence)

Pub/Sub documentation recommends saving replay_id from empty FetchResponse keepalives as well as processed events, because keepalives can advance the replay position and reduce seek time after reconnecting. (low confidence)

Salesforce’s January 2021 CDC-to-Flow example uses an Apex change-event trigger to copy header and changed-field values into a Flow-compatible input class and invoke an autolaunched Flow. Its statement that CDC cannot directly trigger an autolaunched Flow is historical guidance, not proof of current product support. (low confidence)

A channel-member filter can test entity fields and the event header’s change type, but cannot use the array-valued changedFields header. Filtered entity fields are automatically enriched. Consequently, a filter for a target severity value selects current matching state and can also deliver unrelated-field updates; the consumer still needs changedFields qualification to identify severity-field changes. This consequence is a design inference, not a documented transition-filter feature. (high confidence)

Multiple DML operations on the same record within one transaction produce one change event for the initial change type, carrying the final committed data. Salesforce illustrates a Case created at Medium priority and changed to High before commit: the result is one CREATE event with High priority. CDC cannot expose every intermediate severity transition inside that transaction. (low confidence)

Current Salesforce allocation documentation states that CDC has no publishing limit because Salesforce publishes changes automatically. Do not infer a CDC publishing quota from the older design blog’s general discussion of publish and subscribe limits. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
When a relay cannot resume after its last delivered event, its default LATEST recovery starts with new events; EARLIEST resends retained events, whose retention is up to three days. (high confidence)
EventRelayFeedback can be queried for relay status and error messages; no events are forwarded during ERROR, and Salesforce periodically attempts recovery. (low confidence)

Confluent CDC Source can duplicate events after an unexpected stop because it resumes from its last recorded replayID. Events beyond Salesforce’s 72-hour retention window cannot be recovered from that event stream; Kafka ingestion does not remove the upstream outage window. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-11)

A relay in ERROR sends no events and periodically attempts recovery. PAUSED also stops delivery; resumption continues from the prior position only while retained events remain available. Monitor relay state as part of alert delivery operations. (low confidence)

Confluent warns that Source V2 cannot directly migrate CDC Source custom-channel configurations or Streaming API replay-ID semantics. It requires idempotent downstream applications during cutover to handle potential duplicates. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-11)

The routing object's readiness flag describes readiness to route work to an agent; when true, the PendingServiceRouting record cannot be edited. This is routing readiness, not evidence that a Case lifecycle alert has been delivered. (low confidence)

In a historical Stack Exchange report, a Case user said changing Status to Open or New did not resolve the reported routing-record creation failure. This is an attributed observation, not a verified current Salesforce defect. (low confidence)

PendingServiceRouting readiness indicates whether a work item is ready to be routed to an agent; once true, the PendingServiceRouting record cannot be edited. It does not by itself attest that an agent has accepted the work. (low confidence)

Both APIs can replay retained CDC events after disconnection; Pub/Sub does not uniquely provide replay. The documented retention is three days for CDC and high-volume platform events, and a consumer cannot rely on events remaining after that window. (medium confidence)

Pub/Sub Subscribe still needs connection recovery: an error stops the long-lived connection, and the client must retry Subscribe to create a new connection. Changing the replay position requires a new Subscribe call because only the first FetchRequest replay option is honored. (low confidence)

Recovery options change names when migrating: Streaming API uses a specific replay ID, -1 for new events, and -2 for all retained events; Pub/Sub Subscribe uses CUSTOM with replay_id, LATEST, and EARLIEST respectively. Retrieving all retained events can slow performance in both APIs. (high confidence)

CDC event processing decouples work from the original database transaction; Salesforce’s example uses the change event rather than the original object to start its Apex-to-Flow bridge. (low confidence)

Outbound-message retries can arrive out of order or more than once. Check notification IDs before processing. If the source record changes while the notification is queued, delivery contains the latest data rather than intermediate changes, so this mechanism cannot provide an audit trail. (low confidence)

Treat creation and undeletion qualification separately from update qualification: their Pub/Sub event bodies carry all record fields, and a newly created Case can already have High priority at commit. Decide explicitly whether those events should alert when the desired rule is a severity transition rather than initial high-severity state. (medium confidence)

Replayed enriched fields can contain their latest database values rather than their values when the event was stored, because enrichment is added at delivery. Fields that were actually changed in the event retain the correct changed values. Therefore, do not use an unchanged enriched severity field as historical proof of severity at the time of a replayed event. (low confidence)

A custom Platform Event lets the alert producer define the payload with custom fields, making it suitable for a named Case business alert rather than a raw record delta; this is an architectural inference from the documented event model. (high confidence)

CDC automatically provides record-change notifications rather than requiring a custom event definition and explicit publisher for every notification. Salesforce documents notifications for creates, updates, deletes, and undeletes. (low confidence)

Do not interpret the routing-versus-lifecycle distinction as saying that work status never affects Omni-Channel. Status-based capacity measures accepted-work status, and optional capacity checks before reopening or reassigning work can reroute work when the rep lacks capacity. (low confidence)

In both APIs, the default subscription starts with new events rather than recovering the backlog. A reconnecting consumer should explicitly resume from a saved replay position when it needs missed events. (medium confidence)

Pub/Sub change-event parsing also changes header and date handling: changedFields and nulledFields are included beyond the Streaming API header fields; nulledFields, diffFields, and changedFields require further processing; Pub/Sub dates use Epoch time rather than the Streaming API UTC representation. (low confidence)

For either consumer transport, persist replay positions rather than calculating the next position: replay IDs are opaque, need not be contiguous, and are used to recover retained events after disconnection. (high confidence)

Asynchronous Salesforce processing has no completion-time SLA or consistent latency guarantee. An external case alert design therefore needs an explicit latency expectation and monitoring. (low confidence)

If a SOAP outbound-message endpoint is unavailable, Salesforce retries delivery and drops the message after 24 hours of unsuccessful delivery. This is bounded retry, not indefinite guaranteed delivery. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
The Case object has an associated CaseChangeEvent object, introduced in API version 44.0. This provides the Case-specific CDC event object for lifecycle alert consumers. (low confidence)
Native CDC carries new field values and omits the prior record state. A transition that depends on a specific previous severity therefore needs additional prior-state evidence. (high confidence)

Pub/Sub CDC changedFields, diffFields, and nulledFields are bitmaps, not decoded field-name lists. Decode them against the event schema before testing whether the severity field changed. (low confidence)

CDC collapses multiple operations on the same record within one transaction into one event using the initial change type and final committed values. Salesforce’s example creates a Case, changes its priority from Medium to High before commit, and emits one CREATE event with High priority. An UPDATE-only severity rule therefore excludes this creation scenario and does not observe every internal priority step. (low confidence)

Joe Pugh’s 2020 engineering write-up independently reports that native Salesforce CDC delivers new field values without previous values; this historical observation agrees with the current Salesforce architecture guide. (high confidence)

Before qualifying a severity-field change in a Pub/Sub consumer, decode the changedFields and nulledFields bitmaps against the event schema; the schema can be obtained with GetSchema. Payload field presence alone does not establish a change. (high confidence)

CDC automatically emits record-change notifications for enabled objects; custom Platform Events require an explicit publisher and a custom event definition. For Case alerting, this is the choice between reacting to data changes and publishing a deliberate business signal. (high confidence)
Pub/Sub API supports both high-volume custom Platform Events and CDC events, so choosing between these event models does not require a different subscription API. (high confidence)

High-volume Platform Events and CDC share the event delivery allocation, and each subscribed client adds to usage; switching event type alone does not create an independent delivery budget. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

For a custom Case alert whose consumer needs committed transaction data, configure Publish After Commit. Publish Immediately can emit despite a failed transaction or before its data commits. The event definition’s publish behavior does not apply to messages published with Pub/Sub API. (low confidence)

Salesforce documents Event Relay support for custom high-volume platform events, real-time event monitoring events, and change data capture events; standard platform events and standard-volume custom events are excluded. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
PAUSE preserves relay state; STOP deletes current state. EventRelayFeedback documents that resuming a paused relay continues from the last position only within the retention window. (high confidence)

Confluent documents a fully managed Salesforce Source V2 connector that sends Salesforce data to Kafka, supports real-time CDC through Pub/Sub API, and offers Bulk API 2.0 polling and historical loading. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

OSO’s Apache-2.0 Kafka Connect repository advertises a source using Pub/Sub API for CDC and platform events; this establishes an open-source candidate, not independently verified production reliability. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

Event Relay supports custom high-volume platform events and change data capture events. Its support does not extend to standard platform events or standard-volume custom platform events. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

An Event Relay becomes an EventBridge partner event source. After connecting it to an event bus, EventBridge rules can filter events and route them to targets. This supplies the AWS routing stage for an external case-alert pipeline. (low confidence)

External-routing notifications have a routing-specific lifecycle: new work is sent to the partner application, which matches it to logged-in reps; Salesforce also notifies the partner after acceptance, decline, completion, and rep logout. These documented milestones should not be assumed to enumerate every later Case field change. (low confidence)

Moving a Case change-event consumer from Streaming API to Pub/Sub API requires a wire-format change: CometD/Bayeux and JSON become gRPC/protocol buffers and an Apache Avro binary payload. (high confidence)

A migrated CDC parser must distinguish unchanged fields from cleared values: Streaming API omits null and unchanged record fields, whereas Pub/Sub API includes all record fields and represents unchanged and unpopulated fields as null. (low confidence)

Streaming API documentation now specifies that, starting with API version 68.0, successful /meta/connect responses emit updated per-channel replay IDs in ext.replay[<channel>]. Comparisons claiming CometD never advances a cursor without event payloads must therefore be qualified by API version. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

A CometD GitHub issue reports missed Salesforce events while the client remained subscribed and long polling. The maintainer said the initial evidence could reflect bugs or application mistakes and requested connection-level and DEBUG evidence; the report does not establish a confirmed Salesforce or CometD defect. (low confidence)

Salesforce recommends Pub/Sub API for new external applications consuming platform events or change data capture events. Both Pub/Sub API and Streaming API can consume these event categories. (high confidence)

Switching transport does not extend the documented CDC retention window: Pub/Sub API and Streaming API both support replay of retained change events for 72 hours; Salesforce does not guarantee storage beyond that window. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

narrative.documentConcept: Salesforce Apex CDC triggers and Flow outbound alert delivery
narrative.text: Apex can bridge CDC events to Flow, separating automation from the original save transaction. Flow HTTP callouts depend on transaction boundaries. After-save Flow can also initiate SOAP outbound messages, whose background delivery has bounded retries, duplicates, ordering limitations, and latest-value payloads. These properties matter when choosing an external case-alert path and defining monitoring and latency expectations. The CDC-to-Flow example is historical; it does not establish current direct CDC-trigger support in Flow.

narrative.documentConcept: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification
narrative.text: Case change events provide record-change input for alert qualification. Native CDC omits prior values, so a specific old-to-new severity transition needs retained state or suitable field history. Pub/Sub consumers must decode field-change bitmaps and distinguish unchanged empty values from fields actually nulled. Value filters and enrichment do not establish that severity changed. Transaction consolidation also means a Case created and reprioritized before commit can arrive as a creation with its final priority. The alert specification must define its severity field, target values, required prior state, and treatment of creation.

narrative.documentConcept: Salesforce CDC versus custom Platform Events for Case alerting
narrative.text: CDC automatically reports record changes on enabled objects. Custom Platform Events carry a producer-defined business signal and payload. For Case alerting, CDC avoids custom publishing coverage, while custom events allow a deliberate alert contract. Filtered CDC channels can reduce delivery volume, so selectivity alone does not mandate custom events. Both event types use Pub/Sub API and share the delivery allocation. Custom-event publish timing must match the consumer’s need for committed data. CDC is asynchronous and is not an absolute no-loss guarantee. These are design implications of the documented event models; this probe does not prescribe Case transition rules.

narrative.documentConcept: Salesforce Event Relay and external broker alternatives for case alerts
narrative.text: For case alert delivery outside Salesforce, Event Relay supplies a managed forwarding path to Amazon EventBridge. Kafka connectors supply another integration path, including Confluent’s managed connector and an OSO open-source candidate. Relay recovery options, pause versus stop behavior, and queryable error state affect whether downstream alert processing receives missed events. Broker selection therefore requires explicit recovery and monitoring choices; a connector’s existence or vendor reliability claim does not prove lossless alert delivery.

narrative.documentConcept: Salesforce Omni-Channel routing readiness versus Case lifecycle alerts
narrative.text: Omni-Channel readiness concerns routing work to an agent. Salesforce states that later field changes do not reapply routing logic. External routing exposes work-acceptance, decline and completion notifications, but those milestones do not establish coverage of every Case lifecycle change. Treat routing readiness and alert delivery as separate checks. A historical Case routing-error report illustrates why a visible Case status alone does not prove routing succeeded. The forum observation remains attributed and does not establish a current defect.

narrative.documentConcept: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers
narrative.text: For external Case-event consumers, Streaming API and Pub/Sub differ in protocol, encoding, flow control, and CDC payload semantics. Streaming API uses CometD/Bayeux and JSON; Pub/Sub uses gRPC and Avro payloads with explicit demand. A migration must adapt decoding and field-change handling. Both APIs support replay within retention, so cursor persistence and deliberate restart choices matter with either API. Current Streaming API documentation also describes per-channel cursor updates starting with API version 68.0. Historical missed-event reports provide troubleshooting leads rather than proof of a universal protocol defect.
